executiveSummary: GM1729 passes the deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 identity, full and generalized geometry, 14,017 residents, 29 neighbourhoods, twelve BAG places and five Dutch NWB border links are internally coherent. The road-scope safeguard is also correct: NWB links affect only Mobility and road-logistics Supply and are labelled logical transfer proxies. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Gulpen-Wittem is a hilly, Belgian-border headwater municipality whose documented flood pathways are the transboundary Geul, Gulp, Eyserbeek, Selzerbeek and Mechelderbeek, yet the river preset is titled Rhine, Meuse & IJssel and presents 1.661464 dimensionless flood stress, 8,366 affected people-equivalent and exact eight-service availability at both T+24 and T+72 without selecting a local hydrograph, threshold, footprint, arrival or recession. Eight unrelated hazard families reuse one exact 29-neighbourhood ranking; even a source deliberately placed in the official Vijlnerbos ranks its containing neighbourhood only 22nd. The transport graph ends at the Dutch boundary, omitting Belgian road continuation and the upstream catchment, while the official regional profile explicitly requires cross-border stream, wildfire, toxic-cloud, energy, telecom and transport assessment. Public APIs expose 114 managed-water objects, five combustible-nature polygons, 67 regulated external-safety activities and useful timestamped water, provider, energy, telecom, school and care context, but those registers do not prove physical topology, capacity, live state, backup or restoration. Current observations, official registers, historical reconstructions and synthetic T+72 output must remain separate, and NoData must never become zero or safe.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM1729-CROSSBORDER-001: the municipality and controlling Geul/Gulp catchments cross Belgium, but the model has only Dutch neighbour links and no Belgian hydrometeorological, transport, care or aid nodes.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM1729-FIRE-001: five official combustible-nature polygons are present, yet source containment, fuel, spread, smoke, access, firewater and suppression are not causal inputs.

Municipality-specific correction GM1729-WATERCHAIN-001: public registers identify 111 weirs, two sewer pumps and RWZI Wijlre inside the full boundary, but exact Water/Drainage service values have no catchment, state, capacity, power or backup evidence.
Shared/national release blocker GM1729-SPATIAL-001: eight unrelated hazard families reuse one municipality/neighbourhood seed order rather than hazard-specific surfaces or source containment.
Shared/national release blocker GM1729-RECOVERY-001: exact T+0–72 persistence and recovery are not bound to event-valid hydraulics, access, actions, resources or operator commitments.
Retain the corrected NWB service scope and logical-proxy wording, but never portray the five Dutch road fragments as complete cross-border connectivity or incident-time passability.

Retain direct coastal inundation at zero for this inland preset and describe its remaining output as generic wind exercise only; that scoped zero is not an all-clear for local stream, pluvial or drainage flooding.
Limburg/cross-border: any provincial review must include Walloon and Flemish source coverage and EMRIC/Belgian authority governance, not extrapolate Dutch NoData across the border.

Shared/national: every observation, register, historical footprint, planning layer and scenario output needs publisher, edition/valid/retrieval time, spatial/temporal resolution, licence, coverage, NoData and affectsSimulation metadata.

Reference point [5.901420910102985, 50.79846406800682] lies inside the generated and current full boundary.
The current full PDOK feature 92056066-ef10-5f7e-86a4-fd28826a37c is 2025GM1729, valid 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is coherent, but the generalized map geometry is not catchment, terrain, forest, plume, utility or access geography.
notes: The current full boundary is a MultiPolygon with 3,716 coordinate positions and bounding box [5.819409552936704, 50.75036749286346, 5.983518167118529, 50.84888940367429]; the national overview has 165 positions. The overview is suitable for selection, not hydraulic, fire, plume or exact asset containment.

The municipality contains steep plateaus, slopes and the Geul/Gulp/Eyserbeek/Selzerbeek/Mechelderbeek valleys and borders Belgium. These mechanisms cannot be derived from a centroid or administrative-neighbourhood seed.

Official full-resolution water, forest, external-safety, road and settlement layers have different scale, time, completeness and legal semantics; membership in one layer never establishes live function, exposure or another network's topology.
Walloon historical flood geometry, Dutch water registers and administrative boundaries do not share a scenario clock or completeness rule. Transparent/missing cells remain Unknown.

demography.summary: Headline population and aggregate vulnerability inputs agree with CBS 2025 and neighbourhood totals reconcile within publication rounding.
notes: CBS reports 14,017 residents, density 192 residents/km², 32.0 percent age 65 or older and 2,210 one-person households.
The 29 independently rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 14,025 residents, eight above the municipality total (+0.057 percent); they sum to 6,600 households and 4,455 people aged 65 or older.
Largest neighbourhoods are Gulpen 3,465, Wijlre 1,885, Eys-Overeys 1,375, Mechelen 1,290 and Partij-Wittem 775.

Age, household form, car access, density and GP/supermarket distance are aggregate context, not individual medical dependence, tourist/daytime presence, preparedness, evacuation ability or response priority.

regionalDetail.summary: Twenty-nine neighbourhoods provide useful aggregation, but partial attributes and a shared hazard seed make local prioritization physically unsupported.
notes: Core demography and distance fields cover 29/29 neighbourhoods; average home value covers 26/29, cars per household 21/29, benefit shares 26/29 and housing fields 26/29.
District-heating share and public-charging count cover 0/29 and correctly remain null. Missing, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable values are not calculated zeros.
Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have the exact same T+24 rank; compound largely preserves it and earthquake is zero at that checkpoint.
The official stream valleys, combustible-nature polygons and hazardous-activity locations do not drive the local rank, so exact neighbourhood priority is not defensible.

settlements.summary: Twelve BAG woonplaatsen and 58 BRT place features preserve the dispersed-village pattern without inventing service districts.
notes: BAG places are Beutenaken, Elkenrade, Epen, Eys, Gulpen, Heijenrath, Ingber, Mechelen, Reijmerstok, Slenaken, Wijlre and Wittem.
BRT contributes twelve buurtschappen, seven deelkernen, seventeen gehuchten and twenty-two woonkernen, materially important for warning, access and supply planning.
Settlement polygons and labels are context—not evacuation zones, fire sectors, pressure zones, sewer catchments, provider footprints, shelters or resource bases.

transport.summary: Dutch N278/N281/N598/N595 corridor identity and service scope are coherent, but Belgian continuations, internal valley access, incident state and regular-rail semantics are absent.
notes: Five generated NWB border links connect Vaals, Simpelveld, Eijsden-Margraten and Valkenburg aan de Geul on physical road numbers 278, 281, 598 and 595. Twelve source wvk ids are unique; current section-level road numbers were checked rather than inferred from blended labels.
All five links appear only for Mobility and road-logistics Supply, and zero for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom and facilities. This is the correct NWB safeguard.

The graph contains no Belgian node or continuation even though N598/De Plank and local routes cross or depend on Belgium; Flemish and Walloon public registries can supply geometry but not live passability.

Removing the 0.1 km Dutch N598 link at compound T+24 increases municipal pressure by 0.010537 and lowers Mobility/Supply availability by 0.053833/0.033974 while all other services remain exact. This proves model sensitivity, not that the fragment is a complete cross-border route or measured capacity.

The ProRail registry lists Wijlre and Eys-Wittem under the third-party Zuid-Limburgse Stoomtrein Maatschappij, so they must not be presented as proof of regular passenger-rail continuity. Fifty contained GTFS stop areas are scheduled context, not operating service or emergency capacity.
The deployed NDW snapshot assigns no current record to GM1729. A filtered no-match is not evidence that a road, bridge, bus route or Belgian continuation is open.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong public water, nature-fire, industrial, provider and cross-border context exists, but no source supplies complete live topology, resources or first-72-hour state.
notes: The deployed HWH/DAMO cache assigns 114 objects inside the full boundary: 111 weirs, two sewer pumps and RWZI Wijlre. Geometry/status fields do not establish catchment connectivity, compatible capacity, controls, reserve, power/backup or present operation.

The official combustible-nature WFS returns Eperbos, Vijlnerbos, Struchterveld, Schweiberger bos en Kruisbos and Groote Bosch. These polygons are static eligibility/context, not fuel moisture, ignition, spread, smoke, access or suppression state.

The live REV query returns 67 contained regulated activities: 64 propane/propeen tank activities, Brand Bierbrouwerij ammonia cooling, one LPG fuel activity and a Gasunie gas-receiving station. Registration is not an incident, inventory, probability or plume.

At the 6271 NT reference postcode, Netbeheer Nederland shows one Enexis Schoonbron planning-area sample with withdrawal existing/required/queue 77.1/59.0/5.8 MW, injection 76.3/69.6/17.5 MW and ten projects. One planning sample is not municipality coverage, feeder topology, live load, outage or restoration.

RDI contains 59 antenna installations and DUO ten education records; RIVM's dated acute-care questionnaire contains zero in-boundary location. Counts do not establish coverage, backhaul, emergency role, staffing, stock, backup, access or availability; zero care means no listed in-boundary record, not no care dependency.
EMRIC and the regional risk profile establish cross-border coordination mechanisms and risk pathways, not guaranteed crews, ambulances, beds, mutual aid or response times for this selected exercise.

notes: Peak municipal severities are storm 0.696912, pluvial 0.302190, river 0.524133, coastal 0.074090, heat 0.507941, winter 0.605238, cyber 0.502160, earthquake 0.001341, wildfire 0.086099 and compound 0.904482.

Compound T+24 carries 55.719724 mm/h rain, 0.397417 flood stress, 31.423344 m/s wind and 0.440544 cyber disruption. At T+72 rain/wind are zero and cyber is 0.057297, but flood stress remains 0.397417, pressure worsens 0.587638 to 0.592823 and affected increases 8,840 to 8,943.

Heat/drought, storm, winter and cyber trajectories are deterministic exercises without local observation/forecast alignment. Canonical earthquake has zero current shaking at T+24, and canonical wildfire has zero direct flame with 0.129696 smoke and 0.501329 drought; these zeros do not test another local source.
All outputs are synthetic or derived-screening assumptions, not observations, warnings, probabilities, outages, incident intelligence or forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, determinism, exact no-event behavior, cumulative burden, local reconciliation, road-service scope and map-layer invariance pass.

Repeated frames are deterministic; all values are finite/bounded; cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours are monotonic; logical route flow stays within effective capacity.

T+24 local population, affected population and all service demand/delivery ledgers reconcile. Maximum local, demand and delivery floating-point discrepancies are 7.105427357601002e-15, 8.881784197001252e-15 and 7.105427357601002e-15.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard/pressure/affected output unchanged; maximum local layer hazard delta is zero.
All eight pressure weights participate and sum to one; scenario operations/preparedness multipliers remain bounded assumptions rather than inferred public facts.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A shared neighbourhood hash, unselected flood field and ignored fire source create false local precision.
notes: At audit time packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:4402 derives hazardSeed from city seed, scenario seed and region id; model.ts:4414 applies it to all neighbourhoods. Hazard family, source containment, terrain, land cover, catchment and selected public surface are absent.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank BU17290009 Verspreide huizen, Schilberg-Hoogcruts and Eperheide first through third at T+24. Gulpen ranks fifth, Eys-Overeys eighth, Slenaken fourteenth, Epen eighteenth, Mechelen twenty-first, Partij-Wittem twenty-fifth and Wijlre twenty-eighth.
The source-aware expectation is materially different: official evidence places Gulpen at the Gulp/Geul confluence, Wijlre on the Geul, and Mechelen on the Mechelderbeek/Geul pathway.

A controlled source [5.93, 50.76] lies inside official Vijlnerbos and BU17290509. It generates 0.385572 direct fire, but the containing neighbourhood ranks 22nd at hazard 0.373875 while the generic top is 0.471230. The source coordinate does not control local ordering.
GM1729 has no municipality-specific entry in auditedUnsupportedSpatialNotes, so the browser renders exact neighbourhood colours rather than a selected-municipality support warning.

Compound T+24 availability is power 0.304405, water 0.407224, drainage 0.250064, gas 0.580086, telecom 0.215153, mobility 0.824093, facilities 0.349865 and supply 0.421513; at T+72 the first seven worsen slightly while supply rises to 0.423063 without a selected local mechanism.

Public HWH/DAMO, provider, NBNL, RDI, DUO, RIVM and REV sources establish context and hypotheses only. They do not expose complete/safe feeder, pipe, sewer, backhaul, stock, care-routing, live state, backup or restoration topology.

causalTrace.summary: Contributions, dependencies, counterfactuals and logical-proxy metadata reconcile internally, but the local drivers and response claims are not evidence-calibrated.
notes: Municipal pressure uses transparent weights power 0.18, water 0.15, drainage 0.08, gas 0.09, telecom 0.12, mobility 0.12, facilities 0.14 and supply 0.12; the focused gate closes the ledger.

The N598 counterfactual is scoped correctly to Mobility/Supply and the UI calls transfers logical proxies, but its nominal 150 scenario-unit capacity and restriction are synthetic rather than observed throughput/passability.

An exact causal trace can explain model arithmetic; it cannot validate an omitted transboundary catchment, defence/control state, water-chain, fire path, industrial release, road continuation, external care destination or restoration resource.

The regional profile and EMRIC establish conditional coordination roles and cross-border mechanisms, not actual dispatch, accepted assistance, vehicle availability, access, hospital capacity or completion at a checkpoint.

Demand, capacity, backup, network, repair, preparedness, generator-priority and mutual-aid multipliers remain bounded/time-gated scenario assumptions and must never be described as actual crews, assets, operator commitments or household behavior.

recovery72h.summary: Exact persistence, recovery and deterioration through T+72 are not tied to local hydraulics, access, actions, resources or operator commitments.
notes: River T+24 to T+72 freezes flood stress 1.661464, severity 0.524133, pressure 0.563628, affected population 8,366 and every service availability value while cumulative unmet essential-service burden rises 134,464.20 to 536,107.14 person-hours.

No selected rainfall/hydrograph, Belgian inflow, gauge datum/threshold, connected flood footprint, arrival/recession, pump/control state, valley-road access, care destination, stock, crew/material, backup endurance or restoration plan supports these exact paths.

Waterboard projects, municipal policy, regional/EMRIC plans, NBNL projects and road registries are context/doctrine/planning—not proof an action is available, requested, accepted, dispatched, effective or complete.
Waterinfo, KNMI, NDW and any provider observation must remain at its own observation/valid time; none may be silently propagated to the scenario clock or T+72.

evidenceSources.title: Geul catchment system analysis and July 2021 high-water reconstruction
evidenceSources.edition: Water-system analysis published 2023-01-16; July 2021 event reconstruction
supports: Primary official report access page; PDF/download rather than API. No standard reuse licence or fixed update cadence is stated, so it is versioned event/context evidence with affectsSimulation=false until an authority selects and transforms it.

The Geul starts in Belgium near Kelmis/Plombières/Sippenaeken, enters the Netherlands at Cottessen and receives the Gulp, Eyserbeek and Selzerbeek around Gulpen before flowing through Wijlre; the basin is approximately 340 km² and roughly 60 percent lies in the Netherlands.

The analysis uses HBV rainfall-runoff and SOBEK 1D/2D models; Belgian/German areas were represented only in rainfall-runoff components. That modelling boundary and uncertainty must be explicit in any integration.

The detailed report https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/publish/pages/7013/analyse_overstroming_valkenburg.pdf estimates July 2021 peaks near Gulpen of roughly 15 m³/s Gulp, 12 m³/s Eyserbeek and 10 m³/s Selzerbeek and notes gauges failed or exceeded their measuring range. Missing/extreme measurements are uncertainty, never zero.

Historical reconstructed discharge and event maps are not a current observation, probability, forecast or T+72 trajectory. Use only under a named replay/event contract with units, datum, issue/valid time, coverage and NoData.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic municipality contract, reconciliation and road-only service-scope safeguards pass.
findings.evidence: The focused gate executes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services, checks exact zero-intensity behavior, determinism, finite bounds, monotonic event-attributable burden, local demand/delivery reconciliation, all eight pressure contributions and map-layer invariance. Five NWB links appear only for Mobility and Supply; all six other route sets are empty and every transfer is labelled logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain the focused gate, wvk/physical-corridor provenance, service-specific supportedServices rule, logical-proxy wording, zero-intensity semantics and distinct scenario/official-context/observed evidence classes in every correction.

findings.summary: The generalized boundary is appropriate for national selection but not for local hydraulic, forest, plume or route decisions.
findings.evidence: E01's current full boundary has 3,716 coordinate positions versus 165 in the overview. E02/E04 document steep transboundary stream catchments; E07 locates forest and regulated-activity features at finer scale. Administrative polygons contain none of their connectivity, elevation, operating-state or effect semantics.
findings.action: Keep overview geometry for selection/aggregation. Use pinned full official geometry for containment and source-specific hydraulic/fire/effect/route geometry for computation; show edition/generalization and never infer function, exposure or live state from membership alone.

findings.summary: The generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset creates a precise, persistent direct flood in a transboundary Geul/Gulp headwater municipality without selecting the controlling event.
findings.evidence: River T+24 and T+72 both show dimensionless flood stress 1.661464, severity 0.524133, pressure 0.563628, 8,366 affected and identical eight-service availability. The browser clips this to '100% inundation stress' under the Rhine, Meuse & IJssel title. E02/E04 instead document Belgian Geul inflow, Gulp/Eyserbeek/Selzerbeek confluences, Mechelderbeek runoff and extreme-event gauge failure. No rainfall/hydrograph, datum/threshold, connected footprint, depth, arrival, duration, recession or control state is selected.
findings.action: Release gate: suppress the generic direct river amplitude, exact local polygon impacts and dependent service values for GM1729. Do not suppress the real local-stream hazard; show Geul/Gulp/Eyserbeek/Selzerbeek/Mechelderbeek as Unsupported/Unknown until Waterschap Limburg/Belgian partners select a versioned rainfall-runoff/hydraulic event with units, time, coverage and NoData. Retain direct coastal flood zero only as a scoped inland result and label remaining coastal output generic wind exercise, never all-clear.

findings.summary: The pluvial screen ignores documented slope, mud/sediment and local stream pathways and displays unsupported exact neighbourhood impacts.
findings.evidence: E04 states Mechelderbeek drains wooded plateaus to Mechelen/Geul and does not meet a stated 1-in-25 cloudburst handling objective; the draft vision documents steep-slope rapid runoff, water, mud and sediment. Model T+24 reports 0.217200 flood stress and 1,676 affected but uses the exact same local ranking as storm, river, heat, cyber and wildfire; T+72 reports zero rain/flood and zero affected without a local recession or drainage model.
findings.action: Suppress precise pluvial neighbourhood priority until a licensed municipality/water-board stress-test or authority-reviewed model is sampled. Preserve rainfall, surface-runoff, mud/sediment, stream overflow, sewer and groundwater mechanisms separately; use AHN/context only with explicit transformation, and keep transparent/missing coverage Unknown.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazard families reuse one exact neighbourhood order and even an official-forest ignition does not control local allocation.
findings.evidence: model.ts:4402/4414 applies a shared region hash. Eight families rank BU17290009, Schilberg-Hoogcruts and Eperheide first; Wijlre ranks 28th despite its Geul setting. A controlled [5.93, 50.76] source inside E07's Vijlnerbos and BU17290509 produces 0.385572 direct fire, but the source neighbourhood ranks 22nd at 0.373875 while the top reaches 0.471230. GM1729 has no auditedUnsupportedSpatialNotes entry.
findings.action: Release gate: add explicit GM1729 unsupported states and replace the shared rank with hazard-specific samplers: selected hydraulic/cloudburst surface, wind/exposure, heat/land-cover/buildings, cyber service domain, fire eligibility/source/spread/smoke and event-specific ground motion. Tests must enforce rank divergence, source containment/decay where physical, conservation and deterministic Unknown fallback.

findings.summary: The simulation stops at the Dutch boundary although upstream water, roads, wildfire, care, communications and mutual aid are explicitly cross-border.
findings.evidence: E02 traces the Geul from Belgium and says about 40 percent of its basin is outside the Netherlands. E03 requires assessment of foreign rainfall/streams, wildfire, toxic clouds, energy/telecom and transport closure; E05 documents cross-border data/coordination limits. The graph has five Dutch links only, no Belgian node/road continuation, no foreign catchment input and no typed cross-border care/aid resource. EMRIC planning does not guarantee dispatch or response time.
findings.action: Add separate Dutch, Walloon and Flemish source/authority domains; versioned cross-border rainfall/discharge and road geometry; explicit boundary conditions; and typed care/aid/transport/telecom dependencies. Keep registry geometry context-only, resource state proposed/requested/accepted/dispatched/active, and missing foreign coverage Unknown rather than zero.

findings.summary: Five official combustible-nature areas are present, but canonical/local wildfire source, spread, smoke and response remain spatially unsupported.
findings.evidence: E07 identifies Eperbos, Vijlnerbos, Struchterveld, Schweiberger bos en Kruisbos and Groote Bosch. Canonical T+24 has zero direct flame, smoke 0.129696 and drought 0.501329, so it can only be described as synthetic remote smoke. The controlled Vijlnerbos source ranks its own containing neighbourhood 22nd. No current fuel/moisture, wind field, perimeter, cross-border woodland, road access, firewater or suppression state is selected.
findings.action: Retain canonical direct flame zero narrowly and label smoke origin/transport synthetic. Suppress exact local flame/neighbourhood maps unless an official fuel polygon or explicit user source, valid-time weather/fuel assumptions, spread/perimeter/smoke model, access/firewater and bounded response are selected. Static polygon absence or presence never proves safety or active fire.

findings.summary: Relevant hazardous activities are visible only as context and the ten presets have no industrial/technology release pathway.
findings.evidence: E07's exact REV query finds 67 activities, dominated by propane/propeen tanks and including Brand Bierbrouwerij ammonia cooling, LPG and a Gasunie receiving station. The model has no industrial release, fire/explosion/toxic effect, contaminated runoff, isolation or facility-specific service dependency. Registration timestamps/geometry do not prove inventory, incident or probability.
findings.action: Add an explicitly selected industrial/technology scenario family or declare it out of scope near every relevant map. Preserve REV as versioned context; require authority-reviewed generic source term/material, valid-time weather, effect model and action assumptions, and avoid exposing sensitive live inventory/topology.

findings.summary: Exact drinking-water and drainage values are not supported by the registered local stream/sewer/treatment chain or physical utility evidence.
findings.evidence: E08 finds 111 weirs, sewer pumps in Wijlre/Eys and RWZI Wijlre in the deployment cache; E02/E04 establish steep connected streams. River Water/Drainage availability is exactly 0.441211/0.182066 from T+24 through T+72 without catchment, flow direction, controls, capacity, condition, power/backup, potable pressure zone, sewer load, overflow or repair state. Register points are not operation.
findings.action: Separate potable water, wastewater and surface-water control. Retain HWH/DAMO source ids, contributor, retrieval time, licence and full-boundary assignment as context, then seek authority-approved catchment/direction/control/backup data; where unavailable or sensitive use transparent synthetic zones/ranges and Unknown state, never roads or object counts as topology/capacity.

findings.summary: The municipal-node graph cannot represent internal valley access, Belgian route continuity, external acute care or incident-time transit/logistics.
findings.evidence: The five NWB border links omit internal bridges/narrow roads and all Belgian continuations. ProRail points are heritage ZLSM stations; GTFS stop areas are static schedules. Zero assigned NDW and zero in-boundary RIVM acute-care records are no-match semantics, while reference hospitals lie outside. The N598 counterfactual changes Mobility/Supply materially but only restricts a 0.1 km Dutch fragment with synthetic capacity.
findings.action: Retain exact Dutch wvk identity and Mobility/Supply-only scope. Add typed internal critical crossings, Belgian registry continuations, external care/ambulance destinations and scenario access/alternative-route assumptions. Apply NDW/GTFS-RT only in time-aligned observation/replay; capacity, acceptance, vehicle availability, clearance and repair remain Unknown unless confirmed.

findings.summary: Exact first-72-hour persistence and recovery are not bound to local actions, access, resources, controls or operator commitments.
findings.evidence: River T+24 and T+72 freeze every current hazard, pressure, affected and availability value while cumulative burden rises from 134,464.20 to 536,107.14 person-hours. Compound forcing declines but pressure/affected worsen. E03/E05 provide planning roles and cooperation only; E02/E04 document uncertainty and projects, not a selected hydrograph, live control, crew, stock, access or completed action.
findings.action: Add a checkpointed action/resource ledger with proposed/requested/confirmed/dispatched/active/completed/cancelled state; owner/source/jurisdiction, issue/valid/expiry time, delay/ramp, capacity, dependencies, access and uncertainty. Show baseline/no-action counterfactual and sensitivity; generators, backup, repair and mutual aid remain scenario assumptions, never implied actual assets.

findings.summary: Desktop/mobile layout works, but precise unsupported flood output and aggregate warnings can overpower otherwise careful evidence/NoData labels.
findings.evidence: Chromium at 1440×1000 and 390×844 selected GM1729 at river T+72; all eleven map layer buttons activated, no page/local-response error or horizontal overflow occurred, and inspector boxes were 346×742 and 376×560. The hero nevertheless says '100% inundation stress' and derived-screening under a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel banner while rendering precise neighbourhood patches; GM1729 lacks a selected-municipality warning and the mobile user must scroll for detail. Waterinfo correctly shows one level/discharge observation with time/licence/context caveats, but empty NDW/care/drainage/provider fields have different NoData meanings.
findings.action: Add a prominent selected-municipality support banner and suppress precise comparison where the chosen hazard/service lacks its evidence contract. Every map/card/export must distinguish modeled zero, no record, Unknown and not applicable and show publisher, edition/valid/retrieval time, coverage/completeness, licence, unit/confidence and affectsSimulation. Keep responsive sizing, descriptive layer controls and logical-proxy wording; announce scenario/time/layer/support changes for keyboard and screen-reader use.

corrections.summary: Guard GM1729 and replace generic river/pluvial and shared-neighbourhood allocation with authority-selected, source-aware local surfaces.
corrections.validation: GM1729 river direct stress/local impacts are suppressed and local Geul/Gulp/Eyserbeek/Selzerbeek/Mechelderbeek remains Unsupported/Unknown until a versioned event is selected. Tests enforce family-specific ranks, source containment/decay where physical, conservation, deterministic fallback, units/time/coverage/NoData and exact zero-intensity behavior.

corrections.summary: Integrate transboundary catchment and route context without turning register geometry into live state or guaranteed mutual aid.
corrections.validation: Dutch/Walloon/Flemish sources retain jurisdiction, edition, valid/retrieval time, licence, resolution, coverage and NoData. Boundary rainfall/discharge, routes and aid/care are typed separately. Missing foreign data stays Unknown; resource/route state changes simulation only under explicit time-aligned assumptions/observations.

corrections.summary: Build separate potable-water, wastewater and surface-water dependency contracts at safe aggregate resolution.
corrections.validation: HWH/DAMO objects remain CC BY-SA context until catchment, direction, compatible capacity, state, power/backup and authority approval are available. Tests never infer topology from roads/points, expose Unknown/synthetic fallback, and show controlled service changes only for a selected dependency.

corrections.summary: Add source-aware wildfire and an explicit industrial/technology scope.
corrections.validation: A Vijlnerbos source is contained/ranked by selected fuel/source/spread logic; canonical remote smoke stays labelled synthetic. REV/nature registers never imply live incidents. Industrial output requires explicit source/material/weather/effect/action assumptions or is visibly out of scope.

corrections.summary: Represent internal/cross-border access, care and supply nodes while retaining NWB logical-proxy safeguards.
corrections.validation: NWB wvk ids remain section-accurate and affect only Mobility/eligible Supply. Belgian continuations and internal crossings carry separate source/type; NDW/GTFS observations expire; no record is Unknown. Tests vary access/care acceptance and show causal changes without fabricating utilities or guaranteed resources.

corrections.summary: Make first-72-hour action/resource provenance and NoData/support state explicit in model, UI and exports.
corrections.validation: Every action has state, owner, source/jurisdiction, issue/valid/expiry time, delay/ramp, capacity, dependencies, access and confidence; counterfactuals reconcile at all checkpoints. Desktop/mobile show selected-municipality support and distinguish modeled zero/no record/Unknown/not applicable with affectsSimulation.

residualLimitations: Official regional and EMRIC plans establish risks, roles and doctrine, not a current incident, forecast, probability, resource inventory, accepted assistance or municipality-specific loss calibration.

No reviewed source selects a Geul/Gulp/Eyserbeek/Selzerbeek/Mechelderbeek rainfall event, complete Belgian boundary condition, hydrograph/datum, connected footprint, arrival, duration, recession or control/dewatering path for this exercise.
The 2021 Walloon/Dutch event evidence is historical/reconstructed and contains measurement/model uncertainty; it cannot be silently reused as a current forecast or generic probability.

HWH/DAMO, combustible-nature and REV counts are retrieval-time register results and can change; contributors/coverage may be incomplete, and geometry does not establish function, connectivity, inventory or operating state.
The municipal draft vision and completed/planned Slenaken/Mechelderbeek measures are planning/design context, not proof of present performance or guaranteed schedules.

No reviewed public source supplies complete, safe and current electricity feeder, gas/water pipe, valve, sewer catchment, telecom backhaul, backup, stock, crew or restoration topology. Synthetic aggregate fallback must be labelled as such.

The Schoonbron NBNL result is one postcode planning sample and cannot be extrapolated to household service, live load/outage, switching, emergency reserve or T+72 restoration; the precise API licence/stability remain unresolved.

The Epen Waterinfo readings are timestamped point observations. Centimetres NAP are elevation, not flood depth; neither reading supplies a continuous surface, warning threshold, forecast or scenario-clock value.

NWB, Belgian road registries, ProRail and GTFS are physical/registered/scheduled context. They do not establish incident-time passability, regular service, vehicle availability, evacuation throughput, care access, clearance or repair.
The two in-boundary heritage-station registry points must not be interpreted as regular railway service; the fifty GTFS stop areas similarly do not guarantee buses through T+72.
Zero in-boundary acute-care records, zero NDW matches and no drainage provider polygon have different no-record/coverage semantics and are never no dependency, open roads, no drainage or safe.
The controlled Vijlnerbos ignition was a diagnostic sensitivity test, not an incident, forecast or probability; the official forest polygons themselves do not supply current fuel or fire state.

Desktop and mobile smoke tests establish layout/interaction only. They do not certify full WCAG conformance, screen-reader behavior, external-tile uptime or field usability under degraded connectivity.
